record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.context_brief: Strong isospin breaking in gV and gA
record.original_question: In beta-decay effective-field-theory matching from quark-level operators to nucleon-level Lee-Yang couplings, how large are strong isospin-breaking effects from the up-down quark-mass difference on the vector and axial nucleon isovector charges gV and gA when those charges are evaluated at the electron-mass renormalization scale μ = me, and how should those effects be included in comparisons with experiment? Here gX denotes the nucleon matrix element <p|ubar ΓX d|n> for the relevant fermion bilinear ΓX.

evidence.quote: 2. How does (strong) isospin breaking affect gV,A at µ = me?
one introduced the nucleon isovector charges for the different types of fermion bilinear operators, gX = ⟨p|¯uΓX d|n⟩.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. In the low-energy effective field theory of beta decay, quark-level charged-current operators are matched onto nucleon-level operators with Lee–Yang couplings. The nucleon isovector charges are defined by the proton-to-neutron matrix elements
  g_X = ⟨p| ū Γ_X d |n⟩,
where Γ_X ∈ {1, γ^μ, γ^μγ^5, γ^5, σ^{μν}} for the scalar (S), vector (V), axial (A), pseudoscalar (P), and tensor (T) bilinears, respectively. In the exact isospin limit (m_u = m_d, no electromagnetism), the conservation of the vector current implies g_V = 1, while g_A is fixed by QCD dynamics (with current lattice/experimental values g_A ≈ 1.27).

Strong isospin breaking refers to corrections induced by the up–down quark mass difference δm = m_d − m_u (with electromagnetic effects switched off). The charges g_V and g_A depend on the renormalization scheme and scale μ; in the matching to beta-decay observables relevant for low-energy precision tests, the natural reference scale is the electron mass, μ = m_e.

Problem. Determine the size and sign of the strong-isospin-breaking corrections to the nucleon isovector vector and axial charges g_V and g_A induced by the u–d quark mass difference, evaluated in a fixed renormalization scheme at the scale μ = m_e:
 (a) Provide quantitative estimates δg_V^{SIB}(μ = m_e) and δg_A^{SIB}(μ = m_e), with theoretical uncertainties, including the leading second-class-current contribution to g_V (which would otherwise be protected by the Ademollo–Gatto theorem against linear-in-δm corrections).
 (b) Specify how these corrections are to be consistently incorporated when comparing the EFT prediction for neutron and nuclear beta-decay observables (e.g., the neutron lifetime, the axial-to-vector ratio λ = g_A/g_V, correlation coefficients) with experimental measurements, including the separation from electromagnetic isospin breaking and the running from a high matching scale down to μ = m_e.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial estimates exist in the literature: chiral/lattice analyses estimate the u–d mass-difference correction to the vector charge at zero momentum transfer to be of order 3.5×10⁻⁵ (consistent with the Ademollo–Gatto protection), while a leading-order chiral estimate of the strong-isospin-breaking shift in g_A is about −0.0152(53). However, a fully consistent determination at the renormalization scale μ = m_e — separating strong from electromagnetic isospin breaking and prescribing the inclusion in beta-decay observables — is not yet established, and the question is highlighted as an open issue in the modern beta-decay program.

status_evidence.title: Isospin Breaking in the Nucleon Mass and the Sensitivity of β Decays to New Physics
status_evidence.snippet: Isovector scalar/pseudoscalar nucleon charges related to nucleon-mass splittings; isospin breaking traced to u–d mass difference and electromagnetism.
status_evidence.claim: Provides framework relating strong isospin breaking in nucleon charges to the u–d quark mass difference.

status_evidence.title: On the isospin breaking corrections to nuclear beta decay
status_evidence.snippet: Estimate of u–d quark mass difference effect on the neutron beta-decay vector form factor at q^2=0 of order 3.5×10⁻⁵.
status_evidence.claim: Quantifies leading SIB correction to g_V as ~3.5×10⁻⁵, consistent with Ademollo–Gatto.

status_evidence.title: Value of the Axial-Vector Coupling Strength in β and ββ Decays: A Review
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of g_A and corrections including isospin-breaking contributions.
status_evidence.claim: Reports g_A SIB-type contribution at the level of ~−0.015.

status_evidence.title: Precision determination of nucleon iso-vector scalar and tensor charges at the physical point
status_evidence.snippet: Lattice-QCD determinations of nucleon isovector charges in MS-bar at μ = 2 GeV.
status_evidence.claim: Modern lattice computations provide isovector nucleon charges at high μ, requiring running to μ = m_e for beta-decay matching.
